md_description: This DAG represents a workflow for selected medicinal plant specimens used to study alkaloid biosynthetic pathways. It covers sample preparation, genome sequencing, computational identification and annotation of biosynthetic gene clusters, chemical characterization of alkaloids, and integrative analysis linking genomic loci to medically important alkaloid products.

medicinal_plant_specimen.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic specimen metadata: biological identity, taxonomic identity, source material, provenance, and collection context. I excluded extraction, sequencing, capture, chemical processing, and analysis details because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample/subject/experiment identifiers because root-level identifiers are typically generated once and should not be repeated if already_generated contains them; since no already_generated fields were provided here, I still kept the schema focused on non-duplicative specimen descriptors rather than workflow-wide IDs.

md_schema.descr: Accepted scientific name of the medicinal plant specimen, recorded for the material entering the workflow; use standard binomial nomenclature, e.g. 'Papaver somniferum'.
Plant family of the specimen, recorded at the time the biological material is selected; useful for grouping related alkaloid-producing taxa, e.g. 'Papaveraceae'.
Common or vernacular name of the plant specimen, if available, as recorded from the source material label or collection record, e.g. 'opium poppy'.
Type of biological material used from the plant individual, recorded before any processing; indicates the origin of the entity rather than a procedure.
Country where the plant specimen was collected or sourced, recorded from provenance information associated with the biological material.
More specific collection locality for the specimen, such as site, reserve, farm, or garden name; record as free text when available.
Date when the specimen or tissue source was collected, formatted as ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); this is the specimen acquisition date, not a processing date.
Herbarium, voucher, or source repository identifier for the specimen, if preserved; use a stable string identifier, e.g. 'K000123456'.
Whether the specimen was wild-collected, cultivated, or maintained ex situ at the time of sampling; record the provenance state of the biological source.
Developmental stage of the plant specimen at collection, when relevant to alkaloid biosynthesis; record the biological state of the material entering the workflow.
Specific organ or tissue harvested from the plant specimen, if different from the broad specimen_type; record the source material before extraction, e.g. leaf blade or root cortex.
Taxonomic authority string for the scientific name, if curated, e.g. 'L.' or full authority citation; helps disambiguate the specimen identity.
Free-text notes on visible morphology, preservation state, or source context that define the entity itself; do not include processing or assay details.

extract_genomic_dna.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing how genomic DNA extraction was performed: protocol name, key reagents/conditions, tissue input, yield and purity quality indicators, and operator/lab context where needed. I excluded specimen identity fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded sequencing/capture/file fields because those belong downstream on the Capture or Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields by focusing on process-specific parameters rather than sample identifiers or output artifacts.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genomic DNA extraction protocol used for this plant tissue, recorded at the processing step; use a stable method name such as 'CTAB' or 'Qiagen DNeasy Plant Mini Kit'.
Mass of starting plant tissue used for DNA extraction, measured immediately before lysis; report in milligrams and typical values are often 10-500 mg depending on tissue type.
Key composition of the lysis buffer used during DNA extraction, recorded as a process parameter; include major reagents or concentrations such as CTAB, Tris, EDTA, NaCl, and PVP.
Temperature used during tissue lysis or incubation in the DNA extraction process, measured in degrees Celsius at the extraction bench; typical range is 50-80 C depending on protocol.
Duration of the lysis/incubation step during DNA extraction, measured from the start of incubation to quench or transfer; report in minutes and typical range is 10-180 minutes.
General extraction approach used to isolate genomic DNA from plant tissue, recorded as a categorical process descriptor.
Whether an RNase treatment was applied during or after DNA extraction to remove RNA contaminants from the genomic DNA preparation.
Total recovered genomic DNA yield from the extraction, measured after cleanup and before sequencing; report in nanograms, typically from tens to thousands of ng.
A260/A280 absorbance ratio measured on the extracted DNA preparation as a quality indicator for protein contamination; measured after extraction and cleanup, with typical values near 1.8.
Qualitative assessment of DNA integrity after extraction, based on gel electrophoresis, fragment analyzer, or similar QC check; describe whether high molecular weight DNA was recovered.
Role of the person or automated workflow performing the extraction, recorded for process traceability; do not use this for specimen identity.
Date when the DNA extraction was completed, formatted as ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); this is the process completion date, not the specimen collection date.
Free-text notes on deviations, contaminants, or handling details observed during genomic DNA extraction; include only process-relevant observations.

genomic_dna.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the purified genomic DNA material itself: sample identity, concentration, volume, integrity, purity, storage conditions, and chain-of-custody style provenance. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded sequencing platform or file artifacts because those belong downstream to Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating specimen-level identifiers and generic workflow identifiers that should stay at the root Entity node if already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified genomic DNA entity used for sequencing and locus analysis; use a stable lab or LIMS identifier, e.g. 'gDNA_00123'.
Description of the biological source material from which this DNA was purified, recorded as a specimen reference or tissue origin; this is an intrinsic provenance attribute of the DNA entity.
Concentration of the purified genomic DNA sample measured after cleanup and before sequencing setup; report in ng/µL, typically within 1-200 ng/µL.
Total mass of genomic DNA available in the sample at the time of storage or sequencing preparation; report in nanograms, typically tens to thousands of ng.
Usable volume of the purified DNA sample at the time it is entered into sequencing preparation, measured in microliters; typical range is 5-100 µL.
A260/A280 purity ratio of the purified DNA sample measured after extraction; used as an intrinsic quality attribute of the DNA entity, with typical values near 1.8.
A260/A230 purity ratio of the purified DNA sample measured after extraction; indicates residual salt or solvent contamination, with typical values near 2.0-2.2.
Qualitative integrity status of the purified DNA sample prior to sequencing, assessed by gel or fragment analysis; indicates whether the entity is suitable for long-read or short-read sequencing.

Storage temperature of the purified DNA sample while held before sequencing or further analysis, recorded as an intrinsic preservation property of the entity; common values are -20 or -80 degrees Celsius.
Buffer or solvent in which the purified DNA is stored, if applicable; record the medium for the DNA entity, e.g. 'TE buffer' or 'nuclease-free water'.
Number of freeze-thaw cycles experienced by the purified DNA sample before sequencing, used as a stability attribute of the entity; values are typically 0-5.
Whether the purified genomic DNA met the internal QC threshold for proceeding to sequencing and locus analysis, based on concentration, purity, and integrity checks.
Free-text notes describing any unusual properties of the purified DNA entity, such as discoloration, viscosity, or contamination concerns, without describing extraction steps.

dna_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included instrument configuration and measurement-session metadata: platform, manufacturer/model/serial, run chemistry, read setup, loading amount, lane/run identifiers, and active acquisition settings that determine how the DNA was measured. I excluded DNA sample properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded file format, read count, and output quality flags because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided any process-software fields since Capture nodes describe hardware settings rather than computational software.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor description of the device that measured the DNA; e.g. 'Illumina'.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used to capture the genomic DNA signal, recorded for the measurement session; e.g. 'NovaSeq 6000'.
Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session, formatted as the device's manufacturer-assigned string identifier.
Sequencing platform family used for this capture session, recorded as the active measurement technology.
Flow cell or consumable cartridge type loaded for the sequencing capture, recorded at instrument setup; use the platform-specific type name such as 'S4' or 'PromethION R9'.
Sequencing library preparation kit used immediately before the capture session, recorded as the configured chemistry for the instrument run; e.g. a kit name from the vendor.
Target or configured read length for the sequencing run, measured as base pairs per read at capture setup; typical values depend on platform and library design.
Whether the capture session was configured for paired-end acquisition, recorded as the active read mode of the sequencer.
Chemistry or reagent version used for the sequencing capture session, recorded at the instrument configuration step; e.g. a vendor chemistry version code.

Observed cluster density during the sequencing run, if applicable to the platform, measured by the instrument during the capture session; report in thousands of clusters per square millimeter and typical values are platform-dependent.
Concentration of the DNA library loaded onto the sequencing instrument, measured at setup time; report in picomolar and typical values are platform-dependent.
Identifier assigned to the sequencing run or capture session by the instrument or LIMS, used to trace the measurement session; format example 'RUN_2026_001'.
Lane or partition identifier used during the sequencing capture, if the platform supports lane-based acquisition; record the active lane designation at measurement time.
Date and time when the sequencing capture session started, recorded in local instrument time or ISO-8601 format if available; this marks the start of acquisition.
Total elapsed time of the sequencing capture session, measured from instrument start to run completion; report in minutes and typical range depends on platform and run mode.
Whether the sequencing capture completed successfully at the instrument/session level, based on run completion status and basic hardware checks.
Free-text notes on instrument setup, deviations, or session-specific events relevant to the measurement configuration; exclude output file details and biological sample properties.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included raw data artefact properties: file format, file size, read count, base count, read length statistics, storage location, and technical quality metrics that describe the produced sequence files. I excluded instrument configuration and sequencing chemistry because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded assembly or interpretation details because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating DNA sample identifiers or run-session identifiers already owned by upstream Entity/Capture nodes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw sequencing reads produced by the capture step, recorded for the data artefact itself; common values include FASTQ, BAM, or CRAM, with FASTQ typical for primary raw reads.
Storage location or path of the raw sequence read file(s) as deposited in the data system or archive; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
Total size of the raw sequence read file set on disk or in object storage, measured after capture output; report in bytes and typical values range from megabytes to terabytes depending on run scale.
Version of the raw read file format or encoding, if applicable, such as FASTQ encoding version or archive schema version, recorded for the signal artefact.
Total number of reads contained in the raw sequencing signal, counted after demultiplexing or as delivered by the instrument output; typical values are platform- and run-dependent.
Total number of bases in the raw sequencing reads, measured from the produced data artefact; report in base pairs and typically depends on sequencing depth.
Mean read length across the raw sequencing read set, calculated from the raw data artefact; report in base pairs and typical values depend on the sequencing platform.
Read-length N50 of the raw sequence set, calculated from the raw signal artefact as a technical summary of read length distribution; report in base pairs.
Overall GC content of the raw reads, computed directly from the sequence file as a technical compositional metric; report as percent and typical values reflect the plant genome and library bias.
Mean base-call Phred quality score across the raw reads, calculated from the signal artefact as a technical quality metric; typical values are platform-dependent.
Whether the raw sequence read artefact passed the project's technical QC threshold for downstream genome assembly, based on file completeness, yield, and base quality metrics.
Whether the raw read file set has been demultiplexed into sample-specific reads, recorded as an artefact-level processing state of the signal.
Checksum or hash value used to verify integrity of the raw sequence data file, such as MD5 or SHA256 digest, recorded as a stable string identifier.
Free-text notes on technical issues or properties of the raw sequencing artefact, such as adapter carryover, lane imbalance, or partial file transfer.

genome_assembly_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included computational assembly and polishing parameters: assembly software, version, key algorithm settings, read preprocessing choices, polishing rounds, computational resources, and assembly QC thresholds. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded assembled contig/scaffold metrics that are the output properties of the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating generic identifiers already owned by upstream nodes, focusing instead on the reproducible computational procedure and its quality checks.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to reconstruct the plant genome from raw sequencing reads, recorded at the computational process step; e.g. 'SPAdes'.
Version of the assembly software used for genome reconstruction, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '3.15.5'.
Repository or source URL for the assembly software or pipeline code used in this process, recorded when available for reproducibility; use a stable URL string.
Assembly mode or strategy selected for the genome reconstruction process, recorded as a computational setting that affects contig generation; e.g. 'careful', 'metagenome', or platform-specific mode.
Whether adapter trimming or quality trimming was applied to the input reads before assembly, recorded as a process choice within the assembly workflow.
Name of the read trimming tool used before or during assembly, if applicable; record the software actually used in the process, e.g. 'fastp' or 'Trimmomatic'.
Set of k-mer sizes used by the assembler, recorded as a process parameter for de novo assembly; provide as a comma-separated string or pipeline-defined list representation, e.g. '21,33,55'.
Minimum contig length threshold used during assembly filtering or reporting, measured in base pairs and set within the assembly process; typical values are platform- and project-dependent.
Number of polishing iterations applied after initial assembly, recorded as a computational process parameter; typical values are 0-10 depending on sequencing depth and platform.
Name of the polishing tool used to improve assembly accuracy, if applicable; record the software actually used, e.g. 'Pilon' or 'Racon'.
Name of the read-to-assembly alignment tool used during assembly polishing or validation, if applicable; record the software used to map reads back to the assembly.
Number of CPU threads allocated to the assembly process, recorded as a reproducibility parameter for the computational job; typical values depend on cluster resources.
Memory allocated to the genome assembly job, measured in gigabytes and recorded as a computational resource parameter for the process; typical values depend on genome size.
Date and time when the genome assembly computation started, recorded as the process start time in ISO-8601 or local job scheduler format.
Whether the assembly process met the pipeline's internal QC criteria before handoff to downstream genome analysis, based on convergence, coverage, and completeness checks.
Free-text notes on assembly warnings, parameter deviations, or computational issues encountered during genome reconstruction and polishing.

assembled_genome.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included computed assembly-result properties: assembly identifier, contig/scaffold counts and lengths, N50/L50, GC content, completeness/contamination metrics, and validation status that describe the assembled genome output itself. I excluded raw read characteristics because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded assembler software, k-mer settings, and polishing parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided specimen identity fields already handled at the root Entity node and kept the schema focused on the structure and quality of the computed genome product.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the assembled genome derivative, used to track the computed genome product in the data system; use a stable string such as 'asm_0001'.
Storage location of the assembled genome file(s), such as contigs or scaffolds FASTA, recorded for the derivative artifact; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
File format of the assembled genome output, recorded for the derivative artifact; common values include FASTA and GFA.
Total assembled genome size, measured as the sum of contig or scaffold bases in the derivative output; report in base pairs and compare against expected plant genome size.
Number of contigs in the assembled genome output, counted after assembly and filtering; used as a structure metric for the derivative product.
Number of scaffolds in the assembled genome output, if scaffolding was performed; recorded as a structural summary of the derivative genome.
Assembly N50 statistic for the computed genome, measured from contig or scaffold lengths; report in base pairs as a standard continuity metric for the derivative.
Assembly L50 statistic for the computed genome, defined as the number of contigs or scaffolds needed to reach half of the assembly size; a lower value indicates greater continuity.
GC content of the assembled genome sequence, calculated from the derivative output; report as percent and use as a basic compositional metric.

Estimated completeness of the assembled genome, measured after assembly using a completeness assessment method such as BUSCO or k-mer analysis; report as percent and typical values depend on genome quality.
Estimated contamination fraction in the assembled genome derivative, measured after assembly using a contamination assessment method; report as percent and lower values indicate cleaner assemblies.
Whether repetitive sequences were masked in the assembled genome output, recorded as a property of the derivative artifact rather than the assembly process.
Overall validation status of the assembled genome derivative based on downstream quality checks, used to indicate whether the assembly is suitable for gene cluster prediction and annotation.
Free-text notes on assembly fragmentation, unexpected sequence content, or other properties of the computed genome product, excluding process settings and input read details.

biosynthetic_cluster_prediction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included the computational method used to scan the assembled genome for candidate biosynthetic clusters: software name/version, database or rule set, parameter thresholds, organism/domain scope, and process-level confidence/QC indicators. I excluded assembled-genome structure metrics because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the predicted cluster coordinates/counts because those are output properties of the downstream Derivative node. I also kept software provenance fields because, per the schema rules, software name, version, and repository belong on Process nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the biosynthetic gene cluster prediction software used to scan the assembled genome, recorded at the computational process step; e.g. 'antiSMASH'.
Version of the cluster prediction software used in this process, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '7.0'.
Repository or source URL for the cluster prediction software or pipeline code, recorded when available for reproducibility; use a stable URL string.
Reference database or rule set used by the cluster prediction process, if applicable, such as a curated biosynthetic domain database or HMM collection.
Taxonomic scope or organism class targeted by the cluster prediction run, recorded as a process setting if the pipeline supports species-specific models; e.g. 'plants' or 'eukaryotes'.
Minimum genomic span required for a region to be reported as a candidate biosynthetic gene cluster, measured in base pairs and set as a process threshold.
Score or confidence threshold used by the prediction pipeline to call candidate biosynthetic clusters, recorded as a process parameter; the exact scale depends on the software.
E-value cutoff used for hidden Markov model or domain-based detection within the cluster prediction process, recorded as a computational threshold; typical values are software-dependent.
Number of base pairs added upstream and downstream of detected biosynthetic loci when defining candidate cluster boundaries, recorded as a process parameter.
Operational mode used by the prediction pipeline, such as strict, relaxed, or full analysis mode, recorded as the active process configuration.
Whether predicted clusters were manually reviewed or curated after automated detection, recorded as a process-level QC indicator before output handoff.
Date and time when biosynthetic cluster prediction started, recorded as the computational process start time in ISO-8601 or job scheduler format.
Whether the cluster prediction process passed internal QC criteria, such as successful completion and expected output generation, before downstream derivation.
Free-text notes on warnings, parameter deviations, or unusual aspects of the biosynthetic cluster prediction process.

predicted_gene_clusters.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included output properties of the predicted cluster set itself: cluster identifiers, genomic coordinates, strand/context, cluster class, confidence/scores, constituent genes, and output file/storage details. I excluded prediction software, thresholds, and database choices because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded genome assembly properties because those belong to the upstream assembled_genome Derivative node. I also avoided specimen identifiers and workflow-wide IDs already owned elsewhere, focusing on the computed cluster regions as the output artefact.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the set of predicted biosynthetic gene clusters derived from the assembled genome, used to track the derivative result; use a stable string such as 'bgc_set_001'.
Storage location of the cluster prediction output file(s), such as GFF, TSV, or JSON tables, recorded for the derivative artifact; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
File format of the predicted cluster output, recorded for the derivative artefact; common values include GFF, TSV, BED, JSON, and CSV.
Total number of candidate biosynthetic gene clusters identified in the genome, counted in the derivative output after filtering and curation.

Genomic coordinates for each predicted cluster in the assembled genome, recorded as locus intervals in the derivative output; use a standardized interval representation tied to scaffold or contig identifiers.
Length of each predicted cluster region in base pairs, derived from the genomic coordinates in the cluster output; record per cluster or as a summarized list if the schema supports one field.
Strand orientation of the predicted cluster region or its core biosynthetic gene arrangement, if reported by the analysis output; use strand assignments where relevant.
Predicted biosynthetic cluster class or family assigned to each candidate region, such as alkaloid-associated biosynthetic class or broader pathway category, based on the derivative result.
Confidence or score assigned to each predicted cluster in the derivative output, derived from the prediction algorithm's ranking or scoring system; scale is software-dependent.
Number of core biosynthetic genes contained within each predicted cluster, counted from the derivative output and used as a structural summary.
Number of accessory or tailoring genes associated with each predicted cluster, counted from the derivative output when annotated by the predictor.
Identifiers of the genes included in each predicted cluster, recorded as the derivative output's gene membership list; use gene IDs from the assembled genome annotation or predictor output.
Free-text notes on unusual features of the predicted clusters, such as fragmented loci, overlapping predictions, or ambiguous boundary calls.
Whether the predicted cluster output passed the project's QC or curation filter, recorded as an output-level quality indicator for the derivative result.

gene_annotation_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included annotation workflow parameters: annotation software name/version/repository, reference databases, scoring thresholds, evidence sources, and process-level QC. I excluded predicted cluster coordinates and gene membership because those are output properties of the upstream predicted_gene_clusters derivative, and I excluded final enzyme assignments and functional labels because those belong to the downstream annotated_pathway_genes derivative. I also kept software provenance on the process node per the schema rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the gene annotation software used to infer enzyme functions and pathway roles within predicted biosynthetic clusters, recorded at the computational process step; e.g. 'InterProScan'.
Version of the annotation software used in this process, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '6.0'.
Repository or source URL for the annotation software or pipeline code, recorded when available for reproducibility; use a stable URL string.

Reference database or database bundle used to annotate genes in the predicted clusters, recorded as the evidence source for functional inference; e.g. PFAM, InterPro, KEGG, Swiss-Prot, or custom HMM sets.
Release version or build of the reference database used for annotation, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. a date-based or numbered database release.
Primary type of evidence used by the annotation process to assign enzyme functions or pathway roles, recorded as the active annotation mode.
E-value cutoff used when assigning functional annotations from homology or domain matches, recorded as a process threshold; typical values are software- and database-dependent.
Minimum query or domain coverage required for a gene annotation to be accepted, measured as percent and set within the annotation workflow.
Minimum sequence identity required for functional assignment, when applicable, measured as percent and configured in the annotation process.
Whether the annotation workflow attempted to assign biosynthetic pathway roles in addition to general enzyme functions, recorded as a process option.
Whether automated annotations were manually reviewed or curated before downstream use, recorded as a process-level quality indicator.
Date and time when gene annotation started, recorded as the computational process start time in ISO-8601 or job scheduler format.
Whether the gene annotation process passed internal QC criteria, such as successful completion and expected annotation yield, before derivative creation.
Free-text notes on annotation ambiguities, database limitations, or deviations encountered during the functional annotation process.

annotated_pathway_genes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included output properties of the annotated gene set: annotated gene identifiers, assigned enzyme/function labels, pathway role labels, evidence support, confidence, output file details, and summary counts. I excluded annotation software, database versions, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded cluster coordinates and cluster membership because those belong to the upstream predicted_gene_clusters derivative. I also avoided specimen-level identifiers and kept the schema focused on the computed functional gene annotation product.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the annotated pathway gene derivative, used to track the computed annotation product; use a stable string such as 'ann_genes_001'.
Storage location of the annotated gene output file(s), such as TSV, GFF, or JSON tables, recorded for the derivative artifact; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
File format of the annotated gene output, recorded for the derivative artefact; common values include TSV, GFF3, JSON, and CSV.
Total number of genes assigned functional annotations within the predicted biosynthetic clusters, counted in the derivative output after filtering and curation.
Identifier of each annotated gene in the derivative output, matching the genome annotation or cluster prediction gene ID; use a stable gene-level string identifier.
Enzyme or protein name assigned to each annotated gene as part of the derivative result, based on the computational functional inference.
Enzyme Commission number assigned to the annotated gene, if available in the derivative output; use standard EC notation such as '1.14.13.39'.

Biosynthetic role assigned to each annotated gene within the alkaloid pathway, recorded as the computed functional classification in the derivative output; e.g. 'core_biosynthetic', 'tailoring', 'transport', or 'regulatory'.
Primary evidence supporting each gene annotation in the derivative output, such as domain match, sequence similarity, or orthology hit; may be summarized per gene.
Confidence score or support value assigned to each annotated gene function, derived from the annotation output; scale is software- or pipeline-dependent.
Identifier linking each annotated gene to the predicted cluster derivative from which it was derived, used to preserve cluster membership in the annotation output.
Free-text or controlled-text functional description assigned to each gene, such as the inferred catalytic activity or biosynthetic step in the alkaloid pathway.
Whether the annotated gene output passed the project's QC or curation filter, recorded as an output-level quality indicator for the derivative result.
Free-text notes on ambiguous annotations, partial hits, or special cases encountered in the annotated pathway gene output.

plant_material_extraction.reasoning: I fixed the field-id collision by removing extraction_notes, which was already generated earlier in the DAG. I kept the remaining fields within the Process node's semantic territory: extraction protocol, solvent conditions, material/solvent ratios, operating conditions, number of cycles, cleanup/concentration, and process-level yield/QC. I excluded extract identity and downstream analytical artifacts, which belong to the alkaloid_extract Entity and later Capture/Signal nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the solvent extraction method used to recover metabolites from plant material, recorded at the processing step; e.g. maceration, sonication, reflux, or solid-liquid extraction.
Solvent or solvent mixture used to extract alkaloids from the plant material, recorded as the process chemistry; include major components and approximate proportions, e.g. 'methanol:water 80:20'.
Mass of plant material subjected to solvent extraction, measured immediately before extraction; report in milligrams and typical values vary widely by tissue availability.
Volume of extraction solvent used for the plant material, measured in milliliters at the start of extraction; typical values depend on tissue mass and protocol.
Ratio of plant material mass to solvent volume used in the extraction process, recorded as a workflow parameter such as mg/mL or g/mL.

Temperature at which the plant material was extracted, measured in degrees Celsius during the solvent extraction process; typical values range from ambient to elevated temperatures depending on method.
Duration of the solvent extraction step, measured from solvent addition to extraction completion; report in minutes and typical range is 10-1440 minutes depending on protocol.
Agitation or mixing mode used during extraction, recorded as the active process condition; e.g. orbital shaking, stirring, sonication, or static incubation.
Agitation speed used during the extraction process, measured in revolutions per minute when applicable; record only for protocols that specify a set speed.
Number of repeated solvent extraction cycles performed on the same plant material, recorded as a process parameter; typical values are 1-5.
Whether filtration, centrifugation, or cleanup was applied after solvent extraction to clarify the metabolite extract, recorded as a process option.
Method used to concentrate the extract after solvent removal or cleanup, if applicable; e.g. rotary evaporation, lyophilization, or nitrogen stream drying.
Mass of dried or concentrated extract recovered from the plant material at the end of the extraction process; report in milligrams and typical values depend on tissue and solvent.
Whether the extraction process met the project's internal QC criteria for downstream chemical characterization, based on yield, clarity, and handling checks.

alkaloid_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the extract material itself: extract identity, source linkage, matrix/solvent composition, physical appearance, concentration, storage, stability, and aliquot status. I excluded extraction protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream plant_material_extraction Process node, and I excluded analytical instrument settings or spectra because those belong downstream. I also removed any field that would collide with already_generated, specifically avoiding the previously used extraction_notes field and any specimen/root identifiers; the schema focuses on the alkaloid-rich extract as a reusable material entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the alkaloid-rich extract entity used for chemical analysis; use a stable lab or LIMS identifier such as 'ext_alk_0001'.
Reference to the plant specimen from which this extract was prepared, recorded as a provenance link rather than a processing step; use the specimen's stable identifier if available.
Description of the extract matrix or solvent remnant present in the material entity at the time of analysis, e.g. 'methanol extract' or 'dried crude extract'.
Concentration of the alkaloid-rich extract when reconstituted for analysis, measured before instrument injection; report in mg/mL and typical values depend on the analytical method.
Volume of the extract aliquot available for downstream chemical characterization, measured in microliters; typical range depends on preparation scale.
Observed color of the extract material, recorded as an intrinsic appearance attribute of the entity; use descriptive text such as 'amber', 'brown', or 'greenish'.
Observed clarity or turbidity of the extract material prior to analysis, recorded as a material property rather than a process flag; e.g. clear, hazy, or particulate.
Storage temperature of the alkaloid extract material prior to chemical characterization, recorded as an intrinsic preservation property; common values are -20 or -80 degrees Celsius.
Buffer, solvent, or vial medium in which the extract is stored prior to analysis, if applicable; e.g. methanol, acetonitrile, or dry vial storage.
Whether the extract is known or expected to be light sensitive, recorded as a stability attribute of the material entity relevant to metabolite preservation.
Number of freeze-thaw cycles experienced by the extract before analysis, used as a stability attribute of the material entity; typical values are 0-5.
Whether the extract was aliquoted into separate portions for analysis or storage, recorded as a material handling property of the entity.
Overall quality status of the extract material before chemical characterization, based on appearance, concentration, and storage integrity; indicates whether the extract is suitable for analysis.

Free-text notes describing intrinsic properties or visible issues of the alkaloid extract material, such as precipitation, discoloration, or evaporation, without repeating extraction procedure details.

chemical_characterization_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I kept only chemical measurement-session metadata and renamed all colliding generic fields to chemical-specific equivalents to avoid duplication across the DAG. I included the analytical platform, ionization and chromatography settings, acquisition mode, scan range, injection volume, run time, session identifier, and QC/status. I excluded extract properties because those belong to the upstream alkaloid_extract Entity node, and I excluded raw spectra/chromatograms and peak outputs because those belong to the downstream raw_chemical_signal Signal node. I also avoided the previously generated generic instrument/start/notes field names by using chemistry-specific names instead.

md_schema.descr: Analytical platform family used for the chemical capture session, recorded as the active measurement technology for metabolite characterization.

Ionization mode configured for mass spectrometric capture of the extract, recorded at instrument setup; applicable when the platform includes MS. Use values such as positive, negative, dual, or not_applicable.
Chromatography column type or name used during the chemical capture session, recorded as part of the instrument configuration; e.g. C18 reversed-phase column.
Mobile phase composition used for chromatographic separation in the capture session, recorded as the configured solvent system; include major solvents and additives.
Chromatographic gradient or isocratic program used during the analytical capture, recorded as an instrument setting and typically expressed as time versus solvent composition.
Mass-to-charge scan range configured for the capture session, measured in m/z units and relevant to MS-based chemical characterization; record as a range string such as '100-1500'.
Acquisition mode used for the analytical measurement, recorded as the active instrument configuration; e.g. full scan, targeted, data-dependent, or data-independent acquisition.
Volume of extract injected into the analytical instrument for capture, measured in microliters at run setup; typical values depend on platform and method.
Total chromatographic or acquisition time for the chemical characterization session, measured in minutes from injection to completion.
Identifier assigned to the analytical measurement session or run by the instrument or LIMS, used to trace the capture event; format example 'LCMS_RUN_0001'.
Whether the chemical capture session completed successfully at the instrument level and met the project's basic capture QC checks, based on run completion and signal acquisition integrity.
Operational state of the chemical capture session, used to indicate whether the measurement ran as planned or required intervention.
Role of the person or automated workflow operating the chemical capture session, recorded for measurement traceability; do not use this for sample identity.
Free-text summary of any additional instrument settings specific to the chemical measurement session that are not captured in the other fields, such as detector settings or acquisition tweaks.

raw_chemical_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included raw artefact properties of the chemical readout: file format, file size, storage location, scan count, chromatogram/spectrum dimensions, technical quality metrics, and checksum. I excluded instrument configuration and run-session fields because those belong to the upstream chemical_characterization_capture node, and I excluded deconvolution or identification results because those belong downstream to the chemical_processing_process derivative. I also avoided any field names that collided with already_generated, specifically not repeating manufacturer/model/serial, capture start time, or generic notes fields already used elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw chemical readout produced by the analytical capture session, recorded for the signal artefact itself; common values include mzML, mzXML, netCDF, CSV, or vendor-specific formats.
Storage location or path of the raw chemical signal file(s) as deposited in the data system or archive; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
Total size of the raw chemical signal file set on disk or in object storage, measured after capture output; report in bytes and typical values range from megabytes to terabytes.
Total number of scans or spectra contained in the raw chemical signal file, counted from the artefact itself; used as a technical measure of run completeness and acquisition density.
Total number of data points across the raw chromatogram or spectra in the signal file, counted from the artefact; useful for describing data granularity and file complexity.
Observed mass-to-charge range covered by the raw chemical signal artefact, reported as the span present in the file or acquisition output; record as a range string such as '50-1200'.
Total time span of the raw chromatographic signal, measured from the signal artefact itself; report in minutes and typical values depend on the acquisition method.
Maximum base peak intensity observed in the raw chemical signal, recorded as a technical summary of signal amplitude; units are instrument- and software-dependent.
Total ion current integrated from the raw chemical signal artefact, recorded as a technical summary of overall signal abundance; units are instrument- and software-dependent.
Mean signal-to-noise ratio estimated from the raw chemical readout, used as a technical quality metric for the artefact; typical values are method-dependent.
Whether the raw chemical signal artefact passed the project's technical QC threshold for downstream deconvolution and annotation, based on completeness, intensity, and noise checks.
Checksum or hash value used to verify integrity of the raw chemical signal file, such as MD5 or SHA256 digest, recorded as a stable string identifier.
Free-text notes on technical issues or properties of the raw chemical artefact, such as saturation, missing scans, or file transfer problems; avoid repeating instrument settings.

chemical_processing_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included computational workflow parameters for deconvolution and feature detection: software name/version/repository, peak-picking and alignment settings, gap filling, adduct handling, normalization method, and process-level QC. I excluded raw signal file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting feature table and abundance values because those belong downstream to the alkaloid_profile Derivative node. I also avoided colliding with already_generated fields by not repeating generic capture or instrument metadata or notes fields used earlier in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to deconvolve and interpret raw chemical signals into alkaloid features, recorded at the computational process step; e.g. 'MZmine'.
Version of the deconvolution software used in this process, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '3.0' or '3.1'.
Repository or source URL for the deconvolution software or pipeline code, recorded when available for reproducibility; use a stable URL string.
Peak picking or feature detection algorithm used during chemical signal processing, recorded as the active computational method; e.g. centroiding, wavelet, or local minimum based detection.
Minimum intensity or score threshold used to call peaks or features from the raw chemical signal, recorded as a process parameter; scale is software-dependent.
Retention time tolerance used when aligning or matching chemical features across scans or samples, measured in seconds and set within the processing workflow.
Mass-to-charge tolerance used during feature detection or alignment, measured in parts per million and configured as a process parameter.
Whether gap filling was applied during feature table construction to recover missing signals across runs, recorded as a processing option.
Mode used to annotate or collapse adduct relationships during chemical processing, recorded as a workflow setting; e.g. automatic, manual, or disabled.
Method used to normalize feature intensities during chemical processing, recorded as a computational setting; e.g. total ion current, internal standard, or none.
Whether blank subtraction or contaminant filtering was applied during chemical processing, recorded as a process option before output generation.
Date and time when chemical signal processing started, recorded as the computational process start time in ISO-8601 or job scheduler format.
Whether the chemical processing workflow passed internal QC criteria, such as successful feature table generation and acceptable alignment performance, before downstream derivation.
Free-text notes on processing warnings, parameter deviations, or unusual aspects of deconvolution and interpretation; avoid repeating input signal details or output feature values.

alkaloid_profile.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included output properties of the computed chemical feature table: profile identifier, file/storage details, feature counts, m/z and retention-time summaries, abundance metrics, annotation confidence, QC status, and chemical-class summaries. I excluded deconvolution software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream chemical_processing_process node, and I excluded raw signal properties because those belong to the upstream raw_chemical_signal node. I also avoided repeating generic notes fields that collided with already_generated by using profile-specific names only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed alkaloid profile derivative, used to track the feature table output in the data system; use a stable string such as 'alk_profile_001'.
Storage location of the alkaloid feature table output, such as TSV, CSV, JSON, or spreadsheet export, recorded for the derivative artifact; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
File format of the alkaloid profile output, recorded for the derivative artefact; common values include TSV, CSV, JSON, and XLSX.
Total number of chemical features or alkaloid-associated peaks detected in the derivative profile, counted after processing and filtering.
Number of detected features assigned to alkaloid identities or alkaloid-like classes in the profile derivative, counted after annotation.
Total summed abundance of all detected features in the alkaloid profile, measured from the derivative output; units depend on the processing software and detector response.
Method used to scale or normalize feature abundances in the final profile derivative, recorded as an output property; e.g. TIC, internal standard, or none.
m/z values for the detected alkaloid-related features in the derivative output, recorded per feature or in a summarized list representation.
Retention time values for the detected chemical features in the derivative output, measured in minutes and recorded per feature or in a summarized list representation.
Abundance or intensity values for each detected feature in the derivative output, recorded using the normalized scale chosen for the profile.
Confidence score or support value associated with each feature annotation in the derivative output, reflecting how strongly the alkaloid identity or class was supported.
Summary of chemical classes represented in the alkaloid profile, such as predominant alkaloid subclasses or related metabolites, as computed by the derivative pipeline.
Whether the alkaloid profile derivative passed the project's QC or curation filter, recorded as an output-level quality indicator.
Free-text notes on unusual features, missing values, ambiguous annotations, or other properties of the computed alkaloid profile derivative.

integrated_pathway_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included integration workflow parameters: analysis software name/version/repository, input linkage strategy, matching and correlation thresholds, orthology/pathway mapping settings, manual curation options, and process-level QC. I excluded annotated gene and alkaloid profile content because those belong to the upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded final locus-metabolite links because those belong to the downstream pathway_link_analysis Derivative node. I also avoided repeating generic notes identifiers already used elsewhere by using integration-specific field names only.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to jointly analyze annotated biosynthetic genes and alkaloid profiles, recorded at the computational process step; e.g. 'R custom pipeline'.
Version of the integration software or pipeline used in this process, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '4.4' or a pipeline release tag.
Repository or source URL for the integration software or pipeline code, recorded when available for reproducibility; use a stable URL string.
Primary method used to connect annotated genes to alkaloid features, recorded as the active integration strategy; e.g. correlation, rule-based matching, network analysis, or manual curation.
Threshold used to accept a gene-metabolite association based on correlation or similarity, recorded as a process parameter; scale is method-dependent.
Minimum feature abundance or detection threshold required for inclusion in the integrated analysis, recorded as a process cutoff for alkaloid profile filtering.
Relative weighting scheme used to score gene evidence in the integration workflow, recorded as a process parameter; describe how annotations contribute to link inference.
Relative weighting scheme used to score metabolite evidence in the integration workflow, recorded as a process parameter; describe how profile features contribute to link inference.
Whether orthology mapping or cross-species gene comparison was applied during the integration workflow, recorded as a process option.
Whether a network or graph representation was constructed to integrate genes and metabolites, recorded as a process option before derivative output generation.
Whether the integration results were manually reviewed or curated before output, recorded as a process-level quality control option.
Date and time when the integrated pathway analysis started, recorded as the computational process start time in ISO-8601 or job scheduler format.
Whether the integration workflow passed internal QC criteria, such as successful completion and acceptable evidence support, before downstream derivation.
Free-text notes on assumptions, ambiguities, or warnings encountered during the integration of gene annotations and alkaloid profiles.

pathway_link_analysis.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included output properties of the integrated pathway result itself: analysis identifier, output file details, linked cluster/gene/metabolite IDs, inferred pathway labels, association scores, confidence, network/graph summaries, and overall QC. I excluded integration software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream integrated_pathway_analysis Process node, and I excluded the upstream cluster/gene/profile content because those are owned by their respective Derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing generic notes or identifier names that would collide with already_generated by using pathway-link-specific field names only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated pathway link derivative, used to track the computed result in the data system; use a stable string such as 'pathway_link_001'.
Storage location of the integrated pathway analysis output file(s), such as TSV, JSON, or network export, recorded for the derivative artifact; use a stable URI or filesystem path string.
File format of the pathway link output, recorded for the derivative artefact; common values include TSV, JSON, CSV, GEXF, and GraphML.

Identifiers of candidate gene clusters implicated in the integrated pathway result, recorded as the derivative output's cluster membership list; use the stable cluster IDs from the prediction derivative.
Identifiers of annotated genes or enzymes linked to the inferred pathway, recorded in the integrated derivative output; use stable gene IDs from the annotation derivative.
Identifiers or labels of alkaloid features connected to the inferred pathway, recorded in the derivative output; use feature IDs or compound labels from the alkaloid profile.

Name or label assigned to the inferred biosynthetic pathway in the integrated result, recorded as the derivative's scientific interpretation; e.g. a specific alkaloid pathway family or custom pathway label.
Overall score summarizing the strength of the inferred gene-to-metabolite pathway link, calculated in the derivative output; scale is pipeline-dependent.
Confidence value assigned to the integrated pathway inference, recorded as a derivative-level support metric; scale is pipeline-dependent.
Number of independent lines of evidence supporting the inferred pathway link, counted in the integrated derivative output; may include cluster, gene, and metabolite evidence.
Number of nodes in the integrated pathway network or graph, if such a representation was produced, recorded as a derivative output summary.
Number of edges in the integrated pathway network or graph, if such a representation was produced, recorded as a derivative output summary.
Whether the integrated pathway link result passed the project's QC or curation filter, recorded as an output-level quality indicator for the derivative result.
Free-text notes on ambiguous associations, alternative pathway hypotheses, or other observations about the integrated pathway result.
